proprietary.dc:subject: PUBLIC PROCUREMENT
proprietary.dc:description: These Regulations supplement the Procurement Act 2023 (c. 54) (“PA 2023”).

formula.name: enactingText
formula.p:
The Minister for the Cabinet Office makes these Regulations in exercise of the powers conferred by sections 9(2), 33(8), 69(4), 95(1), (2) and (3), 97(1) and (2), 113(1), 115(1), 120(1), 121(1) and (2), 122(3) and 125(1) and (2) of, and paragraph 5(1) of Schedule 1 to, the Procurement Act 2023
2023 c. 54. See section 123(1) of the Procurement Act 2023 for the definitions of “appropriate authority” and “Minister of the Crown”..
These Regulations are made with the consent of the Department of Finance for Northern Ireland in accordance with section 113(4) of the Procurement Act 2023.
The Minister for the Cabinet Office has consulted the following persons on the provision contained in regulation 48 in accordance with section 121(3) of the Procurement Act 2023—

item.p: persons appearing to the Minister to represent the views of private utilities, and
such other persons as the Minister considers appropriate.

formula.p: A draft of this instrument has been laid before, and approved by a resolution of, each House of Parliament pursuant to section 122(4) of the Procurement Act 2023.

content.p: These Regulations may be cited as the Procurement Regulations 2024.

These Regulations, except regulation 48, come into force at the same time at which section 11 of the Procurement Act 2023 comes into force for any purpose
Section 11 comes into force on such day as a Minister of the Crown may by regulations appoint; and different days may be appointed for different purposes. See section 127 of the Procurement Act 2023..
Regulation 48 comes into force on the day after the day on which these Regulations are made.
These Regulations extend to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland, subject to paragraph (2).
Regulation 43 extends to England and Wales only.
Part 5 makes provision about how Parts 2 and 3 apply in relation to Wales and Scotland.

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Publication of notices etc on central digital platform

content.p: A notice, document or information which is published or given in accordance with a provision of the PA 2023 listed in paragraph (3) must be published or given by publishing it on the central digital platform.

The “central digital platform” is the online system established by the Minister for the Cabinet Office and which may be accessed on www.gov.uk
See here: https://www.gov.uk/find-tender.

intro.p: The provisions are—

content.p:
section 15(1) (planned procurement notices)
Planned procurement notices include qualifying planned procurement notices by virtue of section 15(3) of the Procurement Act 2023.,
section 17(1)(a) (preliminary market engagement notices),
section 21(1) (tender notices),
section 24(4) (refining award criteria), in respect of republishing tender notices only,
section 31(5) (modifying a section 19 procurement), in respect of republishing tender notices only,

section 39(2) (dynamic market notices: intention to establish a dynamic market)
Dynamic market notices under section 39(2) include qualifying utilities dynamic market notices by virtue of section 40(6) of the Procurement Act 2023.,
section 39(3) (dynamic market notices: establishment of a dynamic market),
section 39(4) (dynamic market notices: modifications to a dynamic market),
section 39(5) (dynamic market notices: cessation of a dynamic market),
section 44(1) (transparency notices),
section 50(1) (contract award notices),
section 52(3) (key performance indicators),
section 53(1) (contract details notices),
section 53(3) (copies of contracts),
section 55(2) (procurement termination notices),
section 69(1) (payments compliance notices),

p.ins: section 70(1) (information about payments under public contracts),

content.p: section 71(2)(b) (contract performance: information relating to the assessment of performance against key performance indicators),
section 71(5) (contract performance: breach of public contract or failure to perform),
section 75(1) (contract change notices),
section 75(5) (contract change notices: modifications taken together),
section 77(1) (contract modifications),
section 80(1) (contract termination notices),
section 87(1) (below-threshold tender notices),
section 87(3) (contract details notices following notifiable below-threshold contracts),
section 93(2) (pipeline notices), and
section 94(3) (information being withheld).

intro.p: The requirement in paragraph (1) to publish or give a notice, document or information by publication on the central digital platform is met where the contracting authority has submitted the notice, document or information to the platform and—

content.p: the Minister for the Cabinet Office has informed the contracting authority that the notice, document or information has successfully been submitted to the platform, or
the notice, document or information is capable of being accessed by suppliers and members of the public on the platform.

If the central digital platform is unavailable, or all of the conditions in paragraph (6) are met, the contracting authority may publish or give the notice, document or information by publishing the notice, document or information on an alternative online system and in doing so the authority is to be treated as meeting for the time being the requirement in paragraph (1).

intro.p: The conditions are that—

content.p: in the case of a notice mentioned in paragraph (7), no less than 4 hours have passed since the notice was submitted to the central digital platform,
in the case of any other notice, document or information, no less than 48 hours have passed since the notice, document or information was submitted to the platform,
the contracting authority has not received confirmation from the Minister for the Cabinet Office that the notice, document or information has successfully been published on the platform, and
the notice, document or information is not capable of being accessed by members of the public on the platform.

intro.p:
The notice is a transparency notice
For an index of defined expressions related to expressions used in the Procurement Act 2023, certain of which, for example “transparency notice”, are also used in these Regulations, see section 124 of that Act., contract award notice or contract details notice relating to—

content.p: the direct award of a public contract pursuant to regulations made under section 42 of the PA 2023 (direct award to protect life, etc), or
the direct award of a public contract pursuant to paragraphs 13 and 14 of Schedule 5 to the PA 2023 (urgency).

The contracting authority is no longer to be treated as meeting for the time being the requirement in paragraph (1) if the Minister for the Cabinet Office informs the contracting authority that the submission of the notice, document or information to the central digital platform has been rejected.

intro.p: A contracting authority which uses an alternative online system in accordance with paragraph (5) must cooperate with the Minister for the Cabinet Office to ensure that the notice, document or information in question is subsequently—

content.p: published on the central digital platform, and
capable of being accessed by members of the public on the platform.

intro.p: An “alternative online system” is an online system for publishing procurement information which is—

content.p: free of charge and capable of being accessed by suppliers and members of the public,
accessible to people with disabilities, and
not the central digital platform.

Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing the notice, document or information other than on the central digital platform or an alternative online system but the authority must not do so before publishing the notice, document or information on that platform or system.

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Sharing core supplier information through central digital platform

content.p: This regulation applies to a contracting authority where a supplier gives core supplier information to the authority during a procedure listed in paragraph (2) with a view to the award of a public contract.

intro.p: The procedures are—

content.p:
an open procedure
For the meaning of “open procedure” see section 20 of the Procurement Act 2023.,
a competitive flexible procedure,
a direct award under section 41 or 43 of the PA 2023, or
a competitive selection process for frameworks under section 46 of the PA 2023.

If the core supplier information is given during an open procedure or a competitive flexible procedure, the contracting authority must obtain confirmation from the supplier that the supplier has taken the steps set out in paragraph (5) before the end of the tendering period.

If the core supplier information is given before a direct award under section 41 or 43 of the PA 2023, or during a competitive selection process for frameworks under section 46 of that Act, the contracting authority must obtain confirmation from the supplier that the supplier has taken the steps set out in paragraph (5) before the award of the public contract.

intro.p: The steps are—

content.p: the supplier has registered on the central digital platform,
the supplier has submitted its up-to-date core supplier information to that platform, and
the supplier has given that up-to-date core supplier information to the contracting authority by means of a facility provided on that platform for the purpose of sharing core supplier information.

intro.p: Paragraph (7) applies where—

content.p: a supplier has given up-to-date core supplier information to a contracting authority during a procedure listed in paragraph (2), and

the supplier’s core supplier information subsequently changes and the supplier gives updated or corrected core supplier information to the contracting authority before the award of the public contract.
The contracting authority must obtain a further confirmation from the supplier that the supplier has taken the steps set out in paragraph (8) before the award of the public contract.

intro.p: The steps are—

content.p: the supplier has submitted the updated or corrected core supplier information to the central digital platform, and

the supplier has given the updated or corrected core supplier information to the contracting authority by means of a facility provided on that platform for the purpose of sharing core supplier information.

intro.p: In these Regulations “core supplier information” means—

content.p: the supplier’s basic information set out in regulation 9,
the supplier’s economic and financial standing information set out in regulation 10,
the supplier’s connected person information set out in regulation 11, and
the supplier’s exclusion grounds information set out in regulation 12.
In this regulation “tendering period” has the meaning given by section 54(5) of the PA 2023.

In this regulation a reference to a facility provided on the central digital platform includes a reference to a facility to download information to be forwarded on to a contracting authority by a supplier.
This regulation is subject to regulation 7.

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Core supplier information: platform not working, urgency, private utilities

content.p: Where, in respect of core supplier information given during an open procedure or a competitive flexible procedure, a contracting authority cannot obtain confirmation from the supplier that the supplier has taken the steps in regulation 6(5) before the end of the tendering period due to the reason in paragraph (2), paragraph (3) applies.

The reason is that the supplier could not reasonably register on, submit information to, or use a facility for giving information through, the central digital platform because that platform was not working properly during any period before the end of the tendering period.

The contracting authority must obtain confirmation from the supplier that the supplier has taken the steps set out in regulation 6(5) as soon as practicable and in any event before the award of the contract.

p.ins: Paragraph (4A) applies in the case of—
a direct award of a public contract pursuant to regulations made under section 42 of the PA 2023 (direct award to protect life, etc), or
a direct award of a public contract pursuant to paragraphs 13 and 14 of Schedule 5 to the PA 2023 (urgency).
Regulation 6 is to be read as if—

the reference in paragraph (4) to the contracting authority obtaining confirmation before the award of the public contract were a reference to the authority obtaining confirmation as soon as practicable and in any event before the date when the contract details notice is published, and
paragraphs (6) to (8) were omitted.

content.p: Regulation 6 does not apply to a private utility in the case of a direct award of a public contract pursuant to paragraphs 13 and 14 of Schedule 5 to the PA 2023 (urgency).

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Unique identifiers and exemption from publishing them on alternative online system

intro.p: In these Regulations, “unique identifier” means—

content.p: in the case of a procurement, the unique code allocated by the central digital platform when the first notice relating to the procurement is published on that platform, other than in the circumstances set out in paragraph (b),

in the case of a procurement where there has been a switch to a direct award in accordance with section 43 of the PA 2023, the unique code allocated by the central digital platform when the transparency notice relating to the contract is published on that platform,
in the case of a contract, the unique code which enables a reader of a notice referring to the contract to distinguish the contract from other contracts awarded under the same procurement procedure,

intro.p: in the case of a dynamic market, the unique code allocated by the central digital platform when the first of the following notices is published on that platform in relation to the dynamic market—

content.p: any pipeline notice,
any preliminary market engagement notice, or
the first dynamic market notice, and

intro.p: in the case of—

content.p: a supplier,
a contracting authority,
a person carrying out a procurement, or part of a procurement, on behalf of a contracting authority, or
a person other than a contracting authority who is establishing a dynamic market in accordance with section 35(3) of the PA 2023,

wrapUp.p: the unique code which is submitted to the central digital platform and is recognised by that platform or, where no such code is submitted and recognised, is the unique code which is allocated by that platform when the person registers on that platform.

content.p: Paragraph (3) applies where a contracting authority publishes a notice, document or information mentioned in regulation 5(3) on an alternative online system under regulation 5(5).

This regulation sets out the supplier's basic information.

content.p: the supplier’s name,
the unique identifier for the supplier,
the supplier’s contact postal address and email address,
where the supplier has a website, the website address,

the supplier’s VAT registration number (within the meaning of section 5A of the Value Added Tax Act 1994
1994 c. 23. Section 5A was inserted by the Taxation (Post-transition Period) Act 2020 (c. 26).), if applicable, and

intro.p: details of any relevant qualification or trade assurance held by the individual, including—

content.p: in the case of a qualification, the name of the person or body which awarded the qualification, the name of the qualification and the date it was awarded, and
in the case of a trade assurance, the name of the person or body which awarded the assurance, the assurance reference number and the date the assurance was given.

intro.p: Where the supplier is not an individual, the information is—

content.p: the supplier’s name,
the unique identifier for the supplier,
the supplier’s registered or principal office address,
the supplier’s contact postal address and email address,
where the supplier markets its goods, services or works online, the relevant website address,
the supplier’s legal form and the law by which it is governed,

where the supplier is a company registered under the CA 2006
2006 c. 46., the date when the supplier was registered under that Act,

the supplier’s VAT registration number (within the meaning of section 5A of the Value Added Tax Act 1994), if applicable,

content.p: in the case of a qualification, the name of the person or body which awarded the qualification, the name of the qualification and the date it was awarded, or

intro.p: whether the supplier is—

content.p:

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Supplier’s economic and financial standing information

content.p: This regulation sets out the supplier’s economic and financial standing information.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: in the case of a supplier whose accounts were required to be audited for both of the supplier’s most recent two financial years in accordance with Part 16 of the CA 2006, a copy of those accounts,

in the case of a supplier whose accounts were required to be audited for the supplier’s most recent financial year in accordance with Part 16 of the CA 2006, but not the financial year immediately preceding that, a copy of those accounts,

in the case of a supplier whose accounts were required to be audited for both of the supplier’s most recent two financial years in accordance with an overseas equivalent to Part 16 of the CA 2006, a copy of those accounts,

in the case of a supplier whose accounts were required to be audited for the supplier’s most recent financial year in accordance with an overseas equivalent to Part 16 of the CA 2006, but not the financial year immediately preceding that, a copy of those accounts, or

intro.p: in the case of any other supplier—

content.p: if the supplier was in business for both of the supplier’s most recent financial years, accounts or other information for both of those years, or

if the supplier was in business for the supplier’s most recent financial year but not the financial year immediately preceding that, accounts or other information for the supplier’s most recent financial year,

wrapUp.p: which is equivalent to information contained in accounts audited in accordance with Part 16 of the CA 2006, so far as those accounts or that other information can reasonably be given.

content.p: In paragraph (2)(a) and (b) “financial year” has the same meaning as in section 390 of the CA 2006.
This regulation sets out the supplier’s connected person information.
The information is the information in this regulation for each connected person of the supplier.

intro.p: Paragraph (4) sets out the information where—

content.p: the supplier is a company registered under the CA 2006,

the connected person is a person with significant control
For the meanings of “significant control” as well as the following terms used in this regulation, see paragraph 45 of Schedule 6 to the Procurement Act 2023. The terms are “director”, “event”, “parent undertaking”, “subsidiary undertaking”, “predecessor company” and “shadow director”. over the supplier, and
the connected person is registrable.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the connected person’s name, date of birth and nationality,
the connected person’s service address,
which of the specified conditions in Part 1 of Schedule 1A to the CA 2006 applies,
the date when the connected person became registrable as a person with significant control, if applicable, and
the name of the PSC register on which the connected person is registered as a person with significant control, if applicable.

intro.p: Paragraph (6) sets out the information where—

content.p: the supplier is a company registered under the CA 2006,
the connected person is a relevant legal entity, and
the connected person is registrable.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the connected person’s name,
the connected person’s registered or principal office address,
the connected person’s service address,
the connected person’s legal form and the law by which it is governed,
which of the specified conditions in Part 1 of Schedule 1A to the CA 2006 applies,
the date when the connected person became registrable as a relevant legal entity, if applicable, ...
the name of the PSC register on which the connected person is registered as a relevant legal entity, if applicable , and
where the connected person is a company registered under the CA 2006, the person’s registration number given under that Act.

intro.p: Paragraph (8) sets out the information where—

content.p: the supplier is a company registered under the CA 2006, and

intro.p: the connected person is—

content.p: a director or shadow director of the supplier, and
an individual.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the connected person’s name, date of birth and nationality,
the connected person’s service address, and
the country or state (or part of the United Kingdom) in which the connected person is usually resident.

intro.p: Paragraph (10) sets out the information where—

content.p: the supplier is a company registered under the CA 2006, and

intro.p: the connected person is—

content.p: a director or shadow director of the supplier, and
not an individual.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the connected person’s name,
the connected person’s registered or principal office address,
the connected person’s service address,
the connected person’s legal form and the law by which it is governed, and
where the connected person is a company registered under the CA 2006, the person’s registration number given under that Act.

intro.p: Paragraph (12) sets out the information where—

content.p: the supplier is a company registered under the CA 2006, and
the connected person is a parent undertaking or a subsidiary undertaking of the supplier.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the name of the connected person,
the connected person’s registered or principal office address,
the connected person’s service address, and
where the connected person is a company registered under the CA 2006, the registration number given under that Act.

intro.p: Paragraph (14) sets out the information where—

content.p: the supplier is a company registered under the CA 2006, and
the connected person is a predecessor company of the supplier.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the name of the connected person,
the connected person’s last registered or principal office address,
where the connected person is a company registered under the CA 2006, the registration number given under that Act, and
the date when the connected person became insolvent and ceased to trade.

intro.p: Paragraph (16) sets out the information where—

content.p: the supplier is not a company registered under the CA 2006, and
the connected person can reasonably be considered to stand in an equivalent position in relation to the supplier as the connected person described in paragraph (3), (5), (7), (9), (11) or (13).
The information is information which can reasonably be considered to be equivalent to that referred to in paragraph (4), (6), (8), (10), (12) or (14) (as the case may be).

intro.p: Paragraph (18) sets out the information for a connected person to whom none of paragraphs (3), (5), (7), (9), (11), (13) or (15) apply—

content.p: with the right to exercise, or who actually exercises, significant influence or control over the supplier, or
over which the supplier has the right to exercise, or actually exercises, significant influence or control.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the connected person’s name,
the connected person’s registered or principal office address,
the connected person’s service address,
the connected person’s legal form and the law by which it is governed,
where the connected person is a company registered under the CA 2006, the registration number given under that Act,
where the connected person is an overseas equivalent to a company registered under the CA 2006, the equivalent to a registration number issued under the CA 2006,
which of the specified conditions in Part 1 of Schedule 1A to the CA 2006 applies, and
the date when the connected person became registrable as a person with significant control, if applicable.

intro.p: In this regulation—
“registrable”—

content.p: in respect of a person with significant control, has the meaning given by section 790C(4) of the CA 2006;
in respect of a relevant legal entity, has the meaning given by 790C(8) of the CA 2006;
“relevant legal entity” has the meaning given by section 790C(6) of the CA 2006;
“service address” has the meaning given by section 1141 of the Companies Act 2006.
Paragraphs (2) to (13A) set out the supplier’s exclusion grounds information.

intro.p: Whether the supplier or a connected person has been convicted of an offence referred to in the following paragraphs of Schedule 6 to the PA 2023—

content.p: paragraph 2 (corporate manslaughter or corporate homicide);
paragraph 3 (terrorism);
paragraphs 4 to 18 (theft, fraud, bribery etc);
paragraphs 19 to 26 (labour market, slavery and human trafficking offences);
paragraphs 27 to 28 (organised crime);
paragraphs 29 to 31 (tax offences);
paragraph 32 (cartel offence);
paragraph 33 (ancillary offences);
paragraph 34 (offences committed outside the United Kingdom).

intro.p: Whether the supplier or a connected person has been the subject of an event referred to in the following paragraphs of Schedule 6 to the PA 2023—

content.p: paragraph 36 (penalties for transactions connected with VAT fraud and evasion of tax or duty);
paragraph 37 (penalties payable for errors in tax documentation and failure to notify and certain VAT and excise wrongdoing);
paragraph 38 (adjustments for tax arrangements that are abusive);
paragraph 39 (finding by HMRC, in exercise of its powers in respect of VAT, of abusive practice);
paragraph 40 (defeat in respect of notifiable tax arrangements);
paragraph 41 (competition law infringements);
paragraph 42 (equivalents outside the United Kingdom).

intro.p: Whether, in respect of paragraph 43 of Schedule 6 to the PA 2023 (failure to cooperate with investigation)—

content.p: an appropriate authority has given the supplier or a connected person notice under section 60(6) of the PA 2023, and
the supplier or connected person has failed to comply with the notice before the end of the period specified in the notice.

intro.p: Whether the supplier or a connected person has been the subject of an event referred to in the following paragraphs of Schedule 7 to the PA 2023—

content.p: paragraph 1 (orders relating to labour market misconduct);
paragraph 4 (offence relating to environmental misconduct);
paragraph 5 (insolvency bankruptcy etc);
paragraph 6 (suspension or ceasing to carry on all or a substantial part of business);
paragraph 9 (infringement of Competition Act 1998, Chapter II prohibition or equivalent outside United Kingdom);
paragraph 11(2) (court etc ruling of professional misconduct);
paragraph 12 (breach of contract and poor performance).

intro.p: Whether, in respect of paragraph 2 of Schedule 7 to the PA 2023 (labour market misconduct), the supplier or a connected person—

content.p: has been, or is being, investigated for conduct outside the United Kingdom that could result in an order mentioned in paragraph 1 of Schedule 7 to the PA 2023 being made if the conduct occurred in the United Kingdom, or
has engaged in such conduct.

intro.p: Whether, in respect of paragraph 3 of Schedule 7 to the PA 2023 (labour market misconduct), the supplier or a connected person—
has been, or is being, investigated for conduct (whether in or outside the United Kingdom) constituting (or that would, if it occurred in the United Kingdom, constitute) an offence referred to in—

content.p:
section 1, 2, 4 or 30 of the Modern Slavery Act 2015
2015 c. 30.,

section 1, 4 or 32 of the Human Trafficking and Exploitation (Scotland) Act 2015
2015 asp 12., or

section 1, 2 or 4 of the Human Trafficking and Exploitation (Criminal Justice and Support for Victims) Act (Northern Ireland) 2015
2015 c. 2 (N.I.)., or paragraph 16 of Schedule 3 to that Act, or
has engaged in such conduct.

intro.p: Whether, in respect of paragraph 7 of Schedule 7 to the PA 2023 (potential competition infringements)—
the supplier or a connected person has been, or is being, investigated over whether an agreement or concerted practice to which the supplier or a connected person is party has infringed—

content.p:
the Chapter I prohibition (within the meaning given by section 2 of the Competition Act 1998
1998 c. 41.), or
any substantially similar prohibition applicable in a jurisdiction outside the United Kingdom, or
an agreement or concerted practice to which the supplier or a connected person is party has infringed such prohibitions,

wrapUp.p: except in the circumstances mentioned in sub-paragraph (2) of paragraph 7.

intro.p: Whether, in respect of paragraph 8 of Schedule 7 to the PA 2023 (potential competition infringements), the supplier or a connected person—
has been, or is being, investigated over whether the supplier or a connected person has infringed—

content.p: the Chapter II prohibition (within the meaning given by section 18 of the Competition Act 1998), or
any substantially similar prohibition applicable in a jurisdiction outside the United Kingdom, or
has infringed such prohibitions.

intro.p: Whether, in respect of paragraph 10 of Schedule 7 to the PA 2023 (potential competition law infringements), the supplier or a connected person—
has been, or is being, investigated for conduct constituting—

content.p:
an offence under section 188 of the Enterprise Act 2002 (cartel offence)
2002 c. 40., or
a substantially similar offence under the law of a country or territory outside the United Kingdom, or
has engaged in such conduct,

wrapUp.p: except in the circumstances mentioned in sub-paragraph (2) of paragraph 10.

intro.p: Whether, in respect of paragraph 11 of Schedule 7 to the PA 2023 (professional misconduct), the supplier or a connected person—

content.p: has been, or is being, investigated for professional misconduct which brings into question the supplier’s integrity, or
has engaged in such misconduct.

intro.p: Whether, in respect of paragraph 13 of Schedule 7 to the PA 2023, the supplier or a connected person—

content.p: has been, or is being, investigated over whether the supplier acted improperly in relation to any procurement, and in so doing, put itself at an unfair advantage in relation to the award of a public contract, or
has acted improperly in that way.

intro.p: If the supplier or one or more connected persons has been the subject of an event mentioned in paragraphs (2) to (12), the following information in respect of each person who has been the subject of an event—

content.p: a short description of the event,
the name of the person who is the subject of the event,
the person’s name, contact postal address and email address,

intro.p: in the case of a conviction or other event where there is a recorded decision of a public authority which is the authoritative basis for the conviction or other event—

content.p: a link to the web page where the decision can be accessed, or
a copy of the decision, and
if the circumstances which led to the event have ended, the date when they ended.

p.ins: If the supplier or one or more connected persons has been the subject of an event mentioned in paragraphs (2) to (12), any evidence that the supplier or connected person—

took steps to prevent the event occurring again, for example by changing staff or management, or putting procedures or training in place, and
committed to taking further preventative steps, where appropriate.

intro.p: For the meaning of “event”—

content.p: in relation to a provision of Schedule 6 to the PA 2023, see paragraph 45 of that Schedule;
in relation to a provision of Schedule 7 to the PA 2023, see paragraph 16 of that Schedule.

intro.p: In these Regulations, “contracting authority information” means—

content.p: where there is one contracting authority for a procurement, the name of the contracting authority,

intro.p: where there are two or more contracting authorities acting jointly for a procurement—

the name of each of the other contracting authorities,
a contact postal address and email address for the contracting authority or for each contracting authority acting jointly,
the unique identifier for the contracting authority or for each contracting authority acting jointly,

intro.p: for any person carrying out the procurement, or part of the procurement, on behalf of the contracting authority or one or more of the contracting authorities acting jointly—

content.p: the person’s name,
the person’s contact postal address and email address,
the person’s unique identifier, and
a summary of the person’s role, and
in respect of a notice published by the contracting authority, the name, contact postal address and email address of the person who should be contacted in the event of an enquiry about the notice.

intro.p: In these Regulations, “contract subject-matter” means the following information, so far as it is known to the contracting authority when the information is published—

content.p: whether the contract is mainly for the supply of goods, services or works,
a description of the kinds of goods, services or works which will be supplied,
a summary of how those goods, services or works will be supplied,
the estimated date when, or period over which, the goods, services or works will be supplied,
the estimated amount of goods, services or works which will be supplied,
the relevant CPV codes, and
the geographical classification, where it is possible to describe this.

content.p:
the area where the goods, services or works are to be supplied in the United Kingdom, by reference to the relevant ITL 1, ITL 2, and ITL 3 areas listed on the webpage entitled “International Geographies” on the website for the Office for National Statistics

where the goods, services or works are to be supplied outside the United Kingdom, the name of the country and, where appropriate, the region where they are to be supplied.
This regulation sets out what information must be included in a pipeline notice published under section 93(2) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is, for each procurement set out in the pipeline notice—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the title of the procurement,
the unique identifier for the procurement,
the contract subject-matter, and

intro.p: the estimated date when the following will be published—

content.p: the tender notice for the public contract, or
the transparency notice for the public contract.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other relevant information in the notice.
This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a planned procurement notice published under section 15(1) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the title of the procurement,
the unique identifier for the procurement,
the contract subject-matter,
the estimated date when the tender notice for the public contract will be published,
the estimated date by when suppliers will be asked to submit requests to participate in any tender procedure or tenders,

intro.p: which of the following procedures is expected to be used—

content.p: an open procedure, or
a competitive flexible procedure,
whether the public contract will be awarded by reference to suppliers’ membership of a dynamic market,
the estimated date when the public contract will be awarded,
how documents relating to the procurement may be obtained,
a statement explaining how and when an interest in the contract may be expressed, and

as much of the information relating to tender notices which is referred to in regulation 18(2), 19(2), 20(2), 21(2) or 22(2) (as the case may be) that is available to the contracting authority at the time of publishing the planned procurement notice.

This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a preliminary market engagement notice published under section 17(1)(a) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the title of the procurement,
the unique identifier for the procurement,
the contract subject-matter,

intro.p: either—

content.p: the date when the contracting authority intends to close the preliminary market engagement, or
the date when the preliminary market engagement closed, and

content.p: the location, date and time of events, and
any periods for the submission of expressions of interest and information by suppliers.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.
This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a tender notice for the award of a public contract through an open procedure published under section 21(1) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the title of the procurement,
the unique identifier for the procurement,
a statement that the tender notice is for the award of a public contract through an open procedure in accordance with section 20(1) and (2)(a) of the PA 2023,

intro.p:
whether the tender notice relates to a special regime contract

content.p: a concession contract,
a defence and security contract,
a light touch contract, or
a utilities contract,
the contract subject-matter,
the estimated value of the public contract,

intro.p: where the public contract is for goods, services or works which the contracting authority expects will be needed after the expiry of the contract—

content.p: whether the contracting authority intends to carry out a subsequent procurement of similar goods, services or works in reliance on the direct award justification in paragraph 8 of Schedule 5 to the PA 2023, or
an estimate, if possible, of the date when any subsequent tender notice will be published,
whether an electronic auction will be used and, if so, the technical details of how suppliers may participate in the electronic auction,
how tenders may be submitted and the date by when they must be submitted,
the award criteria, or a summary of the award criteria, for the public contract,
the languages in which tenders or enquiries in connection with the tendering procedure may be submitted,
whether the public contract is a contract for which the United Kingdom has obligations under the GPA,

from the date when the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership enters into force for the United Kingdom, whether the public contract is a contract for which the United Kingdom has obligations under that Agreement,

intro.p: whether the public contract is awarded by reference to lots and, if so, for each lot—

content.p: the title of the lot,
the distinct number given to the lot by the contracting authority,

intro.p: the following information, so far as it is known to the contracting authority when the tender notice is published—

content.p: a description of the kinds of goods, services or works which will be supplied,
a summary of how those goods, services or works will be supplied,
the estimated date when, or period over which, the goods, services or works will be supplied,
the estimated amount of goods, services or works which will be supplied,
the estimated value of the lot,
the relevant CPV codes,
the relevant award criteria in relation to the lot,
any option in relation to the lot, and
the geographical classification, where it is possible to describe this,

intro.p: Where the public contract is awarded by reference to lots—

content.p: whether a supplier may only submit a tender for a maximum number of lots and, if so, the maximum number,
whether a supplier may only be awarded a maximum number of lots and, if so, the maximum number, and
whether the authority will award multiple lots to the same supplier in accordance with criteria and, if so, a summary of the criteria,

where the contracting authority considers under section 18(2) of the PA 2023 that the public contract could be awarded by reference to lots but it is not, the reasons for this, except in the case of a utilities contract or a light touch contract,

intro.p: a description of any option which will be included in the public contract—

content.p: to supply additional goods, services or works, or
to extend or renew the term of the contract,

intro.p: whether the contracting authority proposes to set the shortest minimum tendering period by reference to one of the following entries in the table in section 54(4) of the PA 2023 and, if so, which entry—

content.p: entry 2 (certain contracts awarded by a contract authority which is not a central government authority subject to a negotiated tender period);
entry 3 (certain contracts awarded by a contracting authority which is not a central government authority where tenders may be submitted only by preselected suppliers);
entry 4 (a qualifying planned procurement notice has been issued);
entry 5 (state of urgency),

intro.p: whether the contracting authority considers that the public contract or any lot forming part of the contract may be particularly suitable to be awarded—

content.p: to a small and medium-sized enterprise, or
to a non-governmental organisation that is value-driven and which principally reinvests its surpluses to further social, environmental or cultural objectives,

intro.p: whether associated tender documents are being provided in accordance with the tender notice at the same time that the notice is published and, if so—

whether each associated tender document is attached to the tender notice, and
if an associated tender document is not attached to the tender notice, a link to the web page where it is provided,
a description of any technical specifications which are expected to be met or a cross reference to where they can be accessed,
a description of any conditions of participation under section 22 of the PA 2023,
any payment terms (in addition to those mentioned in section 68 of the PA 2023),

intro.p: a description identifying any risk that—

content.p: the contracting authority considers could jeopardise the satisfactory performance of the public contract, but because of its nature, may not be addressed in the public contract as awarded, and

the estimated date when the public contract will be awarded.

Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.
This regulation does not apply to a tender notice for the award of a framework through an open procedure (see instead regulation 20).

a statement that the tender notice is for the award of a public contract through a competitive flexible procedure in accordance with section 20(1) and (2)(b) of the PA 2023,

where the tender notice is being used for the purpose of inviting suppliers to submit a request to participate, how requests to participate may be submitted and the date by when they must be submitted,

intro.p: whether the tender notice is being used—

content.p: to reserve a contract to supported employment providers in accordance with section 32 of the PA 2023, or

whether an associated tender document is being, or may be, provided in accordance with the tender notice after the date when that notice is published and, if so, a link to the web page where it will be provided, or an explanation of how the document will be provided.

intro.p: This regulation does not apply to—

content.p: a tender notice for the award of a framework through a competitive flexible procedure (see instead regulation 20), or
a tender notice for the award of a public contract by reference to suppliers’ membership of a dynamic market (see instead regulation 21).

the term of the framework,

a maximum number of suppliers, or
an unlimited number of suppliers,
