content.p: the unique identifier for the dynamic market against which the public contract is being awarded,
a statement that the tender notice is for the award of a public contract which is to be awarded by reference to suppliers’ membership of a dynamic market, and

intro.p: where the public contract is being awarded under an appropriate part of a dynamic market—

content.p: the title of the part, and
the distinct number given to the part by the person who established the dynamic market.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Tender notices: dynamic markets except qualifying utilities dynamic markets

content.p: This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a tender notice for the award of a public contract by reference to suppliers’ membership of a dynamic market published under sections 21(1)(b) and 34(1) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the same information referred to in regulation 19(2),
the unique identifier for the dynamic market against which the public contract is being awarded,
a statement that the tender notice is for the award of a public contract which is to be awarded by reference to suppliers’ membership of a dynamic market, and

intro.p: where the public contract is being awarded to suppliers that are members of an appropriate part of a dynamic market—

content.p: the title of the part, and
the distinct number given to the part by the person who established the dynamic market.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from providing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.
This regulation does not apply to a tender notice for the award of a framework by reference to suppliers’ membership of a dynamic market (see instead regulation 20).
This regulation does not apply to a tender notice of the type mentioned in regulation 22(1).

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Tender notices: qualifying utilities dynamic market notices

content.p: This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a tender notice for the award of a public contract by reference to a utilities dynamic market established under a qualifying utilities dynamic market notice provided under section 40(2) or (3) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the unique identifier for the dynamic market against which the public contract is being awarded,
the contract subject-matter,

where the public contract is for goods, services or works which the contracting authority expects will be needed after the expiry of the contract, an estimate, if possible, of the date when any subsequent tender notice will be provided,

intro.p: a description of any option which will be included in the public contract—

content.p: to supply additional goods, services or works, or
to extend or renew the term of the contract,
whether an electronic auction will be used,
how requests to participate may be submitted and the date by when they must be submitted,
how tenders may be submitted and the date by when they must be submitted,

intro.p: whether the contracting authority proposes to rely on one of the following minimum tendering periods mentioned in the table in section 54(4) of the PA 2023 and, if so, which one—

content.p: entry 1 (contract being awarded is a light touch contract);
entry 2 (utilities contracts or contracts awarded by a contract authority which is not a central government authority subject to a negotiated tender period);
entry 3 (certain contracts awarded by a contracting authority which is not a central government authority where tenders may be submitted only by preselected suppliers);
entry 5 (state of urgency),
a description of the kinds of goods, services or works which will be supplied, and
the estimated amount of goods, services or works which will be supplied.

Where a contracting authority has already published information mentioned in paragraph (2) in the qualifying utilities dynamic market notice to which the tender notice relates in accordance with regulation 25(2)(i)(ii), the contracting authority is not required to provide that information in the tender notice.
In paragraph (2), “electronic auction” has the meaning given by regulation 18(3).
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from providing other information in the notice.
This regulation sets out what information may be included in an associated tender document provided under section 21(3) of the PA 2023 in accordance with a tender notice.

intro.p: The document may include any information supplementing the tender notice including, where appropriate, information duplicating the information mentioned in—

content.p: regulation 18(2),
regulation 19(2),
regulation 20(2),
regulation 21(2), or
regulation 22(2),
This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a below-threshold tender notice published under section 87(1) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the title of the procurement,
the unique identifier for the procurement,
the contract subject-matter,
the estimated value of the contract,
how tenders may be submitted and the date by when they must be submitted,
whether the notice is being used to invite tenders for a special regime contract and, if so, whether that contract is a defence and security contract or a light touch contract,

intro.p: whether the contracting authority considers that the contract or any lot forming part of the contract may be particularly suitable to be awarded—

content.p: to a small and medium-sized enterprise, or
to a non-governmental organisation that is value-driven and which principally reinvests its surpluses to further social, environmental or cultural objectives,
an explanation of the criteria against which the award of the contract will be assessed, ...
a description of any conditions of participation in relation to the award of the contract , ...

p.ins: whether the notice is being used, in accordance with article 3 of the Local Government (Exclusion of Non-commercial Considerations) (England) Order 2025, to reserve a contract—
to suppliers based within the United Kingdom, or
to suppliers based within the local area, and for that purpose, also specify the areas which constitute the local area for the purposes of article 3(5) of that Order
, and
whether the notice is being used to reserve a contract to either or both of the following—
small and medium-sized enterprises;
non-governmental organisations that are value-driven and which principally reinvest their surpluses to further social, environmental or cultural objectives.

content.p: Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Dynamic market notices (including qualifying utilities dynamic market notices)

content.p: Paragraph (2) sets out other information which must be included in a dynamic market notice published under section 39(2) of the PA 2023 (dynamic market notices: intention to establish a dynamic market).

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the name of the person establishing the dynamic market,

intro.p: where there are two or more persons who are jointly establishing the dynamic market—

content.p: the name of the lead person, and
the name of each of the other persons,
a contact postal address and email address for the person establishing the dynamic market or where there are two or more persons jointly establishing the market that information for each such person,
the unique identifier for the person establishing the dynamic market or where there are two or more persons jointly establishing the market the unique identifier for each such person,

intro.p: the name of any person (“A”) establishing the dynamic market on behalf of another person and—

content.p: A’s contact postal address and email address,
A’s unique identifier, and
a summary of A’s role in relation to the dynamic market,
the name, contact postal address and email address of any person who can be contacted in the event of an enquiry about the dynamic market,
the title of the dynamic market,
the unique identifier for the dynamic market,

intro.p: in the case of a qualifying utilities dynamic market notice—

content.p: a statement that only members of the market, or part of the market, will be notified of a future intention to award a contract by reference to suppliers’ membership of the market, or part of the market, and provided with a tender notice in accordance with section 40(1) and (2) of the PA 2023, and
as much of the information as would be published in any tender notice published in accordance with regulation 21(2) that is available when the qualifying utilities dynamic market notice is published,
how documents relating to the dynamic market may be obtained,
how an application to join the dynamic market may be made,
whether the dynamic market is mainly for the supply of goods, services or works,

a description of the kinds of goods, services or works to which the dynamic market relates, given in such detail that a reader of the dynamic market notice can determine if they wish to apply to join the dynamic market, or appropriate part of the market,
the relevant CPV codes,
the conditions for membership of the dynamic market, or part of the market, set in accordance with section 36 of the PA 2023,
a description of the methods that will be used to verify whether a supplier meets those conditions, including any different conditions for different kinds of goods, services or works,
whether the dynamic market may be used to award a public contract for which the United Kingdom has obligations under the GPA,

from the date when the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership enters into force for the United Kingdom, whether the dynamic market is one for which the United Kingdom has obligations under that Agreement,

intro.p: whether the dynamic market may be used to award a special regime contract and, if so, whether that contract is—

content.p: a concession contract,
a defence and security contract,,
a light touch contract, or
a utilities contract,

intro.p: where the dynamic market is divided into appropriate parts for the purpose of excluding suppliers that are not members of an appropriate part—

content.p: the title of each part,
a description of each part including any relevant CPV codes, and
the distinct number given to each part by the person establishing the dynamic market,

information enabling a reader to identify which contracting authorities will, or may apply to, use the dynamic market (either by reference to a list of authorities or a list describing categories of authorities),
the geographical classification, where it is possible to describe this,

intro.p: in the case of a dynamic market with an estimated date when it will cease to operate—

content.p: the estimated date when the dynamic market will be established, and
the estimated date when the dynamic market will cease to operate,

intro.p: in the case of a dynamic market without an estimated date when it will cease to operate—

content.p: the estimated date when the dynamic market will be established, and
a statement that the dynamic market is an open-ended market,

intro.p: in the case of a dynamic market which is not a utilities dynamic market, whether the dynamic market provides for the charging of fees in accordance with section 38(1) of the PA 2023 and if so—

content.p: the fixed percentage to be applied to the estimated value of any public contract awarded to a supplier by reference to the dynamic market, and
any other information needed in order to enable suppliers to understand how fees will be charged, and

intro.p: in the case of a utilities dynamic market—

content.p: whether the utilities dynamic market provides for the charging of fees in accordance with section 38(3) of the PA 2023, and
if so, information needed in order to enable suppliers to understand how fees will be charged.
Paragraph (4) sets out other information which must be included in a dynamic market notice published under section 39(3) of the PA 2023 (establishment of a dynamic market).

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the same information referred to in paragraph (2) (a) to (h),
the date on which the dynamic market was established,

intro.p: for each supplier that is a member of the dynamic market—

content.p: the supplier’s name,
the supplier’s contact postal address and email address,
the unique identifier for the supplier, and

intro.p: whether the supplier is—

content.p: a small and medium-sized enterprise, or
a non-governmental organisation that is value-driven and which principally reinvests its surpluses to further social, environmental or cultural objectives, and
where the dynamic market is divided into parts, the part of which each of those suppliers is a member.
Paragraph (6) sets out other information which must be included in a dynamic market notice published under section 39(4) of the PA 2023 (modifications to a dynamic market).

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the same information referred to in paragraph (2) (a) to (h),
the date from when the modification has effect,

intro.p: if a supplier is being admitted to the market, a statement to that effect and—

content.p: their name, contact postal address, email address and unique identifier, and
where the dynamic market is divided into parts, the part of which the supplier is a member,

intro.p: whether the supplier is—

content.p: a small and medium-sized enterprise, or
a non-governmental organisation that is value-driven and which principally reinvests its surpluses to further social, environmental or cultural objectives,

intro.p: if a supplier is being removed from the market, a statement to that effect and—

content.p: their name, contact postal address, email address and unique identifier, and
where the dynamic market is divided into parts, the part of which the supplier is a member, and
a summary of any other modification being made.
Paragraph (8) sets out other information which must be included in a dynamic market notice published under section 39(5) of the PA 2023 (cessation of a dynamic market).

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the same information referred to in paragraph (2) (a) to (h), and
the date when the dynamic market ceased to operate.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in a dynamic market notice.
This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a transparency notice published under section 44(1) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the title of the procurement,
the unique identifier for the procurement,

in the case of a procurement where there has been a switch to a direct award in accordance with section 43 of the PA 2023, the unique identifier allocated to the procurement before the switch to direct award,

p.ins: in the case of a procurement where the direct award justification at paragraph 8 of Schedule 5 to the PA 2023 applies, the unique identifiers of the earlier competitive tendering procedure (that is the procurement identifier) and contract referred to in paragraph 8(a) of Schedule 5;

content.p: the unique identifier for the contract, if this is known when the transparency notice is published,
the contract subject-matter,

intro.p: whether the contract is a special regime contract and, if so, whether it is—

content.p: a concession contract,
a defence and security contract,
a light touch contract, or
a utilities contract,
whether the contract is being awarded directly to a supplier that is not an excluded supplier because a direct award justification applies in accordance with section 41(1)(a) of the PA 2023,
if sub-paragraph (h) applies, the direct award justification in Schedule 5 to the PA 2023 which applies and an explanation of why the contracting authority considers that it applies,

whether the contract is being awarded directly to a supplier that is an excluded supplier because the contracting authority considers that there is an overriding public interest in awarding the contract to that supplier in accordance with section 41(2) to (5) of the PA 2023,

intro.p: if sub-paragraph (j) applies—

content.p: the offence or other event mentioned in Schedule 6 to the PA 2023 by virtue of which the supplier is an excluded supplier, ...
which ground in section 41(5) of the PA 2023 applies and an explanation of why the contracting authority considers that it applies , and
the direct award justification in Schedule 5 to the PA 2023 which applies and an explanation of why the contracting authority considers that it applies,
whether the contract is being awarded directly to a supplier pursuant to regulations made under section 42 of the PA 2023 (direct award to protect life, etc),
if sub-paragraph (l) applies, the title and registration number of the statutory instrument containing those regulations,
whether the contract is being awarded directly to a supplier that is not an excluded supplier by virtue of section 43 of the PA 2023 (switching to direct award),

if sub-paragraph (n) applies, the reason the contracting authority considers there were no suitable tenders or requests to participate by reference to section 43(2) of the PA 2023 and why it considers that an award under section 19 of that Act is not possible in the circumstances,

intro.p: whether the contract is being awarded by reference to lots and, if so—

content.p: the title of each lot, and
the distinct number given to each lot by the contracting authority,

p.ins: a description of any option which will be included in the contract—
to supply additional goods, services or works, or
to extend or renew the term of the contract,

content.p: the estimated value of the contract,

intro.p: whether the contracting authority considers that the contract or any lot forming part of the contract may be particularly suitable to be awarded—

content.p: to a small and medium-sized enterprise, or
to a non-governmental organisation that is value-driven and which principally reinvests its surpluses to further social, environmental or cultural objectives,

intro.p: a description identifying any risk that—
the contracting authority considers—

content.p: could jeopardise the satisfactory performance of the contract, but
because of its nature, may not be addressed in the contract as awarded, and
may require a subsequent modification to the contract under paragraph 5 of Schedule 8 to the PA 2023 (modification of contract following materialisation of a known risk),
whether suppliers have been selected for the award of the contract,

intro.p: if suppliers have been selected for the award of the contract, for each supplier selected—

content.p: the supplier’s name,

intro.p: the—

content.p: unique identifier for the supplier, or

in the case of a direct award of a public contract pursuant to paragraphs 13 and 14 of Schedule 5 to the PA 2023 (urgency) where the supplier has not been allocated a unique identifier when the transparency notice is published but can instead provide unique information (for example a company registration number given under the CA 2006) which can be recognised by the central digital platform as the basis for a unique identifier allocated by that platform, that unique information, and
the supplier’s contact postal address and email address,
the estimated date when the contract will be entered into, and

intro.p: where the contract is a framework—

content.p: the term of the framework,

whether the framework provides for fees to be charged to a supplier in accordance with the framework and, if so, details of the fixed percentage by which they will be charged in accordance with section 45(7) of the PA 2023, and
the contracting authorities entitled to award contracts in accordance with the framework (whether by listing the names of those authorities or by describing categories of authorities).
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Contract award notices except those published by private utilities

content.p: This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a contract award notice published by a contracting authority under section 50(1) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the title of the procurement,

intro.p: the unique identifier for—

content.p: the procurement,
the public contract,
where the public contract is being awarded in accordance with a framework, the procurement of the framework in accordance with which the public contract is being awarded, and
where the public contract is being awarded by reference to a suppliers’ membership of a dynamic market, the dynamic market,
the contract subject-matter,

intro.p: for each supplier awarded the public contract—

content.p: the supplier’s name,
the supplier’s contact postal address and email address,

intro.p: the—

content.p: unique identifier for the supplier, or

in the case of a direct award of a public contract pursuant to paragraphs 13 and 14 of Schedule 5 to the PA 2023 (urgency) where the supplier has not been allocated a unique identifier when the contract award notice is published but can instead provide unique information (for example a company registration number given under the CA 2006) which can be recognised by the central digital platform as the basis for a unique identifier allocated by that platform, that unique information,
whether the supplier is an association of companies or other consortium,

intro.p: whether the supplier is—

content.p: a small and medium-sized enterprise,
a non-governmental organisation that is value-driven and which principally reinvests its surpluses to further social, environmental or cultural objectives,

a supported employment provider
For the meaning of “supported employment provider” see section 32 of the Procurement Act 2023., or
a public service mutual,
for each associated person of the supplier, the person’s name and contact postal address, and

the supplier’s connected person information in accordance with regulation 11, but reading paragraphs (4)(a) and (8)(a) of that regulation as if each reference to date of birth were a reference to month and year of birth, subject to paragraph (4),
the date when the contracting authority decided to award the public contract,

intro.p: if the public contract is being awarded by reference to lots, for each lot—

content.p: the name of the supplier that is being awarded the lot,
the title of the lot,
the distinct number given to the lot by the contracting authority,
a description of the kinds of goods, services or works which will be supplied,
a summary of how those goods, services or works will be supplied,
the estimated date when, or period over which, the goods, services or works will be supplied,
the estimated amount of goods, services or works which will be supplied,
the estimated value of the lot,
the relevant CPV codes, and
the geographical classification, where it is possible to describe this,

intro.p: where the public contract is being awarded in accordance with a framework, details of which of the following procedures was used—

content.p: a competitive selection process for frameworks under section 46 of the PA 2023, or
an award without further competition under section 45(4) of the PA 2023,

where the public contract is a framework that is being awarded under an open framework, the unique identifier for the procurement of the last framework awarded under the open framework (unless no framework has previously been awarded under the open framework),
where the public contract is being awarded under an appropriate part of a dynamic market, the distinct number given to that part by the person who established the dynamic market,

intro.p: whether the public contract is a special regime contract and, if so, whether it is—

content.p: a concession contract,
a defence and security contract,
a light touch contract, or
a utilities contract,

whether the contracting authority has provided an assessment summary to each supplier that submitted an assessed tender in accordance with section 50(3) of the PA 2023 and, if so, the date when those assessment summaries were provided,
the estimated value of the public contract,

intro.p: in respect of public contracts with an estimated value of £5 million or less—

content.p: the total number of tenders submitted by the contracting authority’s deadline for submitting tenders (discounting tenders submitted but subsequently withdrawn),
the total number of tenders assessed by the contracting authority, and

intro.p: the total number of tenders assessed by the contracting authority which were submitted by—

content.p: a small and medium-sized enterprise, and
a non-governmental organisation that is value-driven and which principally reinvests its surpluses to further social, environmental or cultural objectives,

wrapUp.p: except in the case of a direct award under section 41 or 43 of the PA 2023,

intro.p: in respect of public contracts with an estimated value of more than £5 million—

content.p: the total number of tenders submitted by the contracting authority’s deadline for submitting tenders (discounting tenders submitted but subsequently withdrawn),

intro.p: the name of each supplier that—

content.p: submitted a tender which was assessed for the purposes of determining the most advantageous tender under section 19(1) of the PA 2023, and
was not awarded the public contract,

intro.p: for each unsuccessful supplier—

content.p: the unique identifier for the supplier or other unique information referred to in sub-paragraph (e)(iii)(bb),
the supplier’s postal address,
whether the supplier is a small and medium-sized enterprise, and
whether the supplier is a non-governmental organisation that is value-driven and which principally reinvests its surpluses to further social, environmental or cultural objectives,

wrapUp.p: except in the case of a direct award under section 41 or 43 of the PA 2023,

intro.p: where the public contract is a framework or awarded other than in accordance with a framework, details of which of the following procedures was used—

content.p: an open procedure,
a competitive flexible procedure, or
a direct award under section 41 or 43 of the PA 2023,
whether a tender notice was used to reserve the contract to supported employment providers in accordance with section 32 of the PA 2023, and whether the contract was awarded to such a supplier,
whether a tender notice was used to reserve the contract to public service mutuals in accordance with section 33 of the PA 2023, and whether the contract was awarded to such a supplier,

the end date of any standstill period under section 51 of the PA 2023 or, if no standstill period applies, any date before which the contracting authority has determined not to enter into the contract,
the estimated date when the contract will be entered into,
where the public contract is being awarded directly under section 41 or 43 of the PA 2023, the same information referred to in 26(2)(h) to (o),

where the public contract is being awarded in accordance with a framework which is arranged by reference to lots, the distinct number given by the contracting authority to the lot under which the contract is being awarded, and

intro.p: where—

content.p: the public contract is being awarded by reference to lots, and

the contracting authority is using the contract award notice to give notice that it is ceasing to procure all of the goods, services and works set out in one or more of those lots or any lots under future contracts under the arrangement under section 18(2)(a) of the PA 2023,

intro.p: “Ceased lot information” is—
the following information for each ceased lot—

content.p: the title of the lot,
the distinct number given to the lot by the contracting authority,
the relevant CPV codes, and
a description of the kinds of goods, services or works which were to have been supplied under the lot, and
the date when the contracting authority decided to cease the procurement under the lot.

intro.p: A contracting authority is not required to publish, in accordance with paragraph (2)(e)(vii), connected person information which is secured information in relation to—

content.p: a connected person who is an individual who meets the description in regulation 11(3)(b) and (c), or
a connected person who is an individual who meets the description in regulation 11(15)(b).

intro.p: “Secured information” is information which—

content.p:
in relation to an individual mentioned in paragraph (4)(a) or (b), is for the time being omitted from a PSC register in accordance with regulation 33(1) of the Register of People with Significant Control Regulations 2016
S.I. 2016/339., or

intro.p: in relation to an individual mentioned in paragraph (4)(b), is information regarding which the individual—

content.p: is reasonably of the view set out in paragraph (6), and
has confirmed that view in writing to the contracting authority.

intro.p: The view is that if the information is published—

content.p: the activities of the company, or
one or more characteristics or personal attributes of the applicant when associated with that company,

wrapUp.p: will put the applicant or a person living with the applicant at serious risk of being subjected to violence or intimidation.

content.p: Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.
This regulation does not apply to a contracting authority which is a private utility.

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Contract award notices published by private utilities

content.p: This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a contract award notice published by a private utility under section 50(1) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the same information referred to in regulation 27(2)(a) to (r), except sub-paragraphs (h), (n) and (o),
the estimated date when the contract will be entered into, and

intro.p: a description of any option in the public contract—

content.p: to supply additional goods, services or works, or
to extend or renew the term of the contract.

Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement (including information that relates to other contracts awarded under the same procurement) in the notice.

intro.p: This regulation does not apply to—

content.p: the direct award of a public contract under section 41 or 43 of the PA 2023 (see instead regulation 29), or
the award of a public contract in accordance with a framework (see instead regulation 30).

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Contract award notices published by private utilities: direct awards

content.p: This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a contract award notice published by a private utility under section 50(1) of the PA 2023 where the contract was awarded directly in accordance with section 41 or 43 of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the same information referred to in regulation 27(2)(a) to (r), except sub-paragraphs (c)(iii) and (iv), (h) to (j), (l), (n) and (o),
the estimated date when the contract will be entered into,

intro.p: a description of any option in the public contract—

content.p: to supply additional goods, services or works, or
to extend or renew the term of the contract,
whether the contract is being awarded directly to a supplier that is not an excluded supplier because a direct award justification applies in accordance with section 41(1)(a) of the PA 2023,
if sub-paragraph (d) applies, the direct award justification in Schedule 5 which applies and an explanation of why the contracting authority considers that it applies,

whether the contract is being awarded directly to a supplier that is an excluded supplier because the contracting authority considers that there is an overriding public interest in awarding the contract to that supplier in accordance with section 41(2) to (5) of the PA 2023,

intro.p: if sub-paragraph (f) applies—

content.p: the offence or other event mentioned in Schedule 6 to the PA 2023 by virtue of which the supplier is an excluded supplier, ...
which ground in section 41(5) of the PA 2023 applies and an explanation of why the contracting authority considers that it applies , and
the direct award justification in Schedule 5 to the PA 2023 which applies and an explanation of why the contracting authority considers that it applies,
whether the contract is being awarded directly to a supplier pursuant to regulations made under section 42 of the PA 2023 (direct award to protect life, etc),
if sub-paragraph (h) applies, the title and registration number of the statutory instrument containing those regulations,
whether the contract is being awarded directly to a supplier that is not an excluded supplier by virtue of section 43 of the PA 2023 (switching to direct award), and

if sub-paragraph (j) applies, the reason the contracting authority considers there were no suitable tenders or requests to partipate by reference to section 43(2) of the PA 2023 and why it considers that an award under section 19 is not possible in the circumstances.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Contract award notices published by private utilities: frameworks

content.p: This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a contract award notice published by a private utility under section 50(1) of the PA 2023 where the contract is being awarded in accordance with a framework.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the same information referred to in regulation 27(2)(a) to (r), except sub-paragraphs (c)(iv), (i), (j), (n), (o) and (p),
the estimated date when the contract will be entered into,

intro.p: a description of any option in the public contract—

content.p: to supply additional goods, services or works, or
to extend or renew the term of the contract,
where the framework is arranged by reference to lots, the distinct number given by the contracting authority to the lot under which the contract is being awarded,

intro.p: details of which of the following procedures was used to award the public contract—

content.p: a competitive selection process for frameworks under section 46 of the PA 2023, or
an award without further competition under section 45(4) of the PA 2023, and
if sub-paragraph (e)(ii) applies, an explanation of why the contracting authority considered that it applies by reference to section 45(4) of the PA 2023.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.
This regulation sets out what information must be included in an assessment summary provided to a supplier under section 50(3) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: In the case of the most advantageous tender, the information is—

content.p: the name of the supplier,
a contact postal address and email address for the supplier,
the unique identifier for the supplier,

intro.p: in respect of the award criteria for the public contract—
the award criteria, including the assessment methodology, set out in full, or a summary of the award criteria including—

content.p: the title of each criterion,
the relative importance of each criterion, and
how each criterion was to have been assessed by reference to scored and what scored were to have been available for each criterion, and
if the award criteria, including the assessment methodology, are not set out in full in the assessment summary, an indication of where the full version can be accessed, and

intro.p: how the tender was assessed against the award criteria by reference to scores including—
the score determined for each award criterion and—

content.p: an explanation for that score by reference to relevant information in the tender, and
where an award criterion includes sub-criteria for assessment, an explanation of how the tender was assessed by reference to each sub-criterion, and
the total score and any sub-total scores.

intro.p: In the case of any other assessed tender, the information is—

content.p: the information referred to in paragraph (2) (a) to (d) in respect of the tender,
the information as referred to in paragraph (2)(e) in respect of the tender, but only to the extent that the tender was assessed against the award criteria,

any further explanation of why the public contract is not being awarded to the supplier including, where the tender was disqualified under the assessment methodology under section 23(3) of the PA 2023, the reasons for that disqualification
the information referred to in paragraph (2)(e) in respect of the most advantageous tender.

All assessment summaries in respect of a public contract which are provided by a contracting authority to suppliers in accordance with section 50(3) of the PA 2023 must be provided to each supplier at the same time.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from providing other information that relates to the same procurement in an assessment summary.

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Contract details notices: open or competitive flexible procedure

intro.p: This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a contract details notice published under section 53(1) of the PA 2023 where the public contract was entered into following—

content.p: an open procedure, or
a competitive flexible procedure (including by reference to a dynamic market).

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the title of the procurement,
the unique identifier for the procurement,
the unique identifier for the public contract,
where the public contract was awarded by reference to suppliers’ membership of a dynamic market, the unique identifier for that dynamic market,
the contract subject-matter,

intro.p: for each supplier party to the public contract—

content.p: the supplier’s name,
the supplier’s contact postal address and email address,
the unique identifier for the supplier, and

intro.p: whether the supplier is—

content.p: a small and medium-sized enterprise,
a non-governmental organisation that is value-driven and which principally reinvests its surpluses to further social, environmental or cultural objectives,
a supported employment provider, or
a public service mutual,

intro.p: whether the public contract was awarded following—

content.p: an open procedure, or
a competitive flexible procedure,

intro.p: whether the contract was reserved—

content.p: to supported employment providers in accordance with section 32 of the PA 2023, or
to public service mutuals in accordance with section 33 of the PA 2023,

intro.p: if the public contract was awarded by reference to a lot—

content.p: the title of the lot,
the distinct number given to the lot by the contracting authority,
a description of the kinds of goods, services or works which will be supplied,
a summary of how those goods, services or works will be supplied,
the estimated date when, or period over which, the goods, services or works will be supplied,
the estimated amount of goods, services or works which will be supplied,
the estimated value of the lot, and
the relevant CPV codes,
the estimated value of the public contract,
the date when the public contract was entered into,

intro.p: a description of any option in the public contract—

content.p: to supply additional goods, services or works, or
to extend or renew the term of the contract,
where the public contract was awarded under an appropriate part of a dynamic market, the distinct number given to that part by the person who established the dynamic market,

intro.p: whether the public contract is a special regime contract and, if so, whether it is—

content.p: a concession contract,
a defence and security contract,
a light touch contract, or
a utilities contract,
whether the public contract is a contract for which the United Kingdom has obligations under the GPA,

from the date when the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership enters into force for the United Kingdom, whether the public contract is a contract for which the United Kingdom has obligations under that Agreement,

where key performance indicators were set in accordance with section 52(1) of the PA 2023, a description of the three key performance indicators which the contracting authority regards, at the time the contract details notice is published, as most material to performance of the contract obligations, and

where key performance indicators were not set by virtue of section 52(2) of the PA 2023, an explanation of why the contracting authority considers that the supplier’s performance under the contract could not appropriately be assessed by reference to key performance indicators.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.
This regulation does not apply to a contract details notice where the public contract is a framework (see instead regulation 33).
This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a contract details notice published under section 53(1) of the PA 2023 where the public contract is a framework.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the same information referred to in regulation 32(2) (a) to (q), except sub-paragraph (h),
the contracting authorities entitled to award public contracts in accordance with the framework (whether by listing the names of those authorities or by describing categories of authorities),
the term of the framework,
whether the framework is awarded under an open framework,

where the framework was awarded under an open framework, the unique identifier for the procurement of the last framework awarded under the open framework (unless no framework has previously been awarded under the open framework),
where the framework was awarded under an open framework, the estimated end date of the open framework,

intro.p: whether the public contract was awarded—

content.p: following an open procedure,
following a competitive flexible procedure, or
directly, in accordance with section 41 or 43 of the PA 2023,

whether the framework provides for fees to be charged to a supplier in accordance with the framework and, if so, details of the fixed percentage by which they will be charged in accordance with section 45(7) of the PA 2023,
the price payable, or mechanism for determining the price payable, under a public contract awarded in accordance with the framework, and
details of the selection process to be applied on the award of a contract in accordance with the framework.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Contract details notices: public contracts awarded in accordance with frameworks

content.p: This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a contract details notice published under section 53(1) of the PA 2023 where the public contract was awarded in accordance with a framework.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the same information referred to in regulation 32(2), except sub-paragraphs (e), (h), (n), (p) and (q),
the unique identifier for the procurement of the framework in accordance with which the public contract is being awarded,
whether the framework is a defence and security framework within the meaning given by section 47(4)(a) of the PA 2023,
where the framework is arranged by reference to lots, the distinct number given by the contracting authority to the lot under which the contract is being awarded,

intro.p: details of which of the following procedures was used to award the public contract—

content.p: a competitive selection process for frameworks under section 46 of the PA 2023, or
an award without further competition under section 45(4) of the PA 2023, and
if sub-paragraph (e)(ii) applies, an explanation of why the contracting authority considered that it applies by reference to section 45(4) of the PA 2023.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.

This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a contract details notice published under section 53(1) of the PA 2023 where the public contract was awarded directly in accordance with section 41 or 43 of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the same information referred to in regulation 32(2), except sub-paragraphs (e), (h) and (n),
whether the contract was awarded directly to a supplier that is not an excluded supplier because a direct award justification applies in accordance with section 41(1)(a) of the PA 2023,
if sub-paragraph (b) applies, the direct award justification in Schedule 5 which applies and an explanation of why the contracting authority considers that it applies,

whether the contract was awarded directly to a supplier that is an excluded supplier because the contracting authority considered that there was an overriding public interest in awarding the contract to that supplier in accordance with section 41(2) to (5) of the PA 2023,

p.ins: if sub-paragraph (d) applies—
the direct award justification in Schedule 5 to the PA 2023 which applies and an explanation of why the contracting authority considers that it applies,
the offence or other event mentioned in Schedule 6 to the PA 2023 by virtue of which the supplier is an excluded supplier, and
which ground in section 41(5) of the PA 2023 applies and an explanation of why the contracting authority considers that it applies,

content.p: whether the contract was awarded directly to a supplier pursuant to regulations made under section 42 of the PA 2023 (direct award to protect life, etc),
if sub-paragraph (f) applies, the title and registration number of the statutory instrument containing those regulations,
whether the contract was awarded directly to a supplier that is not an excluded supplier by virtue of section 43 of the PA 2023 (switching to direct award),

if sub-paragraph (h) applies, the reason the contracting authority considers there were no suitable tenders or requests to participate by reference to section 43(2) of the PA 2023 and why it considers that an award under section 19 of that Act is not possible in the circumstances,
whether the contract was awarded to a supplier that is an excluded supplier by virtue of section 41(2) of the PA 2023, and
if sub-paragraph (j) applies, the offence or other event mentioned in Schedule 6 to the PA 2023 in question.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.
This regulation does not apply to a contract details notice where the public contract is a framework (see instead regulation 33).
This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a contract details notice published under section 87(3) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

the title of the procurement,
the unique identifier for the procurement,
the unique identifier for the contract,

intro.p: for each supplier party to the contract—

content.p: the supplier’s name,
the supplier’s contact postal address and email address,
the unique identifier for the supplier, ... and

intro.p: whether the supplier is—

content.p: a small and medium-sized enterprise, or
a non-governmental organisation that is value-driven and which principally reinvests its surpluses to further social, environmental or cultural objectives,
the contract subject-matter,

intro.p: whether the contract was awarded by reference to lots and, if so—

content.p: the title of each lot under the contract, and
the distinct number given to each lot by the contracting authority,
whether the contract is a defence and security contract or a light touch contract,
the estimated value of the contract,
the date when the contract was entered into, and

content.p: to supply additional goods, services or works, or
to extend or renew the term of the contract.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.

heading.ins: Supplier registration on central digital platform: below-threshold contracts

p.ins: Before the publication of a contract details notice in accordance with section 87(3) of the PA 2023, the contracting authority must obtain from the supplier—
confirmation that the supplier has taken the steps set out in paragraph (2), and
its unique identifier.
The steps are—
the supplier has registered on the central digital platform, and
the supplier has submitted the required information to that platform.
In this regulation “
” means—
the supplier’s name,
the supplier’s contact postal address and email address, and
whether the supplier is—
a small and medium-sized enterprise, or
a non-governmental organisation that is value-driven and which principally reinvests its surpluses to further social, environmental or cultural objectives.

content.p: This regulation sets out what information must be included in a procurement termination notice published under section 55(2) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the title of the procurement,
the unique identifier for the procurement,
a statement to the effect that, following the publication of a tender or transparency notice in respect of a contract, the contracting authority has decided not to award the contract, and
the date when the contracting authority decided not to award the public contract.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in a procurement termination notice.
This regulation sets out what information must be included in a payments compliance notice published under section 69(1) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the dates of the first and the last days of the reporting period to which the payments compliance notice relates,

intro.p: in respect of sums paid by the contracting authority under public contracts during the reporting period—

content.p: the average number of days taken to make those payments, where day 1 is the first day after the invoice day;

intro.p: the percentage of those payments which were made, where day 1 is the first day after the invoice day—

content.p: within the period beginning on day 1 and ending with day 30;
within the period beginning on day 31 and ending with day 60;
on or after day 61,

p.ins: the proportion of invoices paid in accordance with the term in section 68(2) of the PA 2023 during the reporting period, expressed as a percentage of the total number of invoices that were, or should have been, paid in accordance with that term within the reporting period,

content.p: in respect of sums which became payable under public contracts during the reporting period, the percentage of those payments which were not made within the reporting period, and

a statement of the director or similar officer of the contracting authority who is responsible for the contracting authority’s finances setting out that they approve the payments compliance notice and that person’s name and job title.

intro.p: In paragraph (2)—

content.p: “average” means the arithmetic mean;
“invoice day” means the day on which a contracting authority receives an invoice.

intro.p: For the purposes of paragraph (2), a payment is made—

content.p: when it is received by the supplier;
if there is any delay in the sum being received for which the contracting authority is not responsible, when it would have been received without that delay.

In paragraph (3) the reference to a contracting authority receiving an invoice includes the invoice being delivered to an address, or through an electronic invoicing system, as specified in the contract in question for that purpose.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other relevant information in the notice.

p.ins: This regulation sets out what information about a payment must be published under section 70(1) of the PA 2023 (“the payment information”).
The payment information is—
in respect of the contracting authority which made the payment—
the name of the contracting authority,
a contact postal address and email address for the contracting authority,
the unique identifier for the contracting authority,

if different from sub-paragraph (a), the information referred to in that sub-paragraph in respect of the contracting authority which published the contract details notice under section 53 of the PA 2023 in respect of the relevant contract,
the unique identifier for—
the procurement, and
the relevant contract,
in respect of each payment to which the payment information relates—
the name of the supplier to whom the payment was made, and
the unique identifier for the supplier to whom the payment was made,
the value of the payment net of VAT, and
the date when the payment was made.
A unique identifier is not required to be published by virtue of paragraph (2)(c) or (d)(ii) if—
no notice relating to the relevant contract has been previously published on the central digital platform, and
the unique identifier is not available.
In paragraphs (2)(b), (c) and (3), the relevant contract is the public contract under which the payment to which the payment information relates was made.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other relevant information alongside the payment information.

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Contract performance notices except in relation to full termination

intro.p: This regulation makes provision about information published under either of the following provisions—

content.p: section 71(2)(b) of the PA 2023 (assessment of performance against key performance indicators);
section 71(5) of that Act (breach of public contract or failure to perform).
The information must be published in the form of a notice called a “Contract Performance Notice”.
Where the information is being published under section 71(2)(b) of the PA 2023, the notice must include the information set out in paragraph (4).

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the title of the procurement,

intro.p: the unique identifier for—

content.p: the procurement, and
the public contract,

p.ins: a description of the three key performance indicators set in accordance with section 52(1) which the contracting authority regards, at the time the contract performance notice is published, as most material to performance of the contract obligations,
a statement that the notice is being used to set out the contracting authority’s assessment of performance against key performance indicators selected in accordance with sub-paragraph (d),

intro.p: for each supplier whose performance has been assessed against the selected key performance indicators—

content.p: the supplier’s name,
the supplier’s contact postal address and email address, and
the unique identifier for the supplier,
the contracting authority’s assessment of performance against the selected indicators in accordance with the ratings set out in paragraph (5), and
the time period to which the contracting authority’s assessment applies.
The ratings are—

td.p: Performance is meeting or exceeding the key performance indicators
Performance is close to meeting the key performance indicators
Performance is below the key performance indicators
Performance is significantly below the key performance indicators
Performance cannot be described as good, approaching target, requires improvement or inadequate

content.p: Where the information is being published under section 71(5) of the PA 2023, the notice must include the information set out in paragraph (7).

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the title of the procurement,

intro.p: the unique identifier for—

content.p: the procurement, and
the public contract,

intro.p: for each supplier that has committed the breach or failure to perform set out in the notice—

content.p: the supplier’s name,
the supplier’s contact postal address and email address, and
the unique identifier for the supplier,

intro.p: the information referred to in—

content.p: section 71(5)(a) of the PA 2023 (that section 71(5) of that Act applies), and
section 71(5)(b) of the PA 2023 (the circumstances giving rise to the application of section 71(5) of that Act),

intro.p: a statement that the information is being published because—

content.p: the supplier has breached the public contract and the breach resulted in one of the events referred to in section 71(3)(b), or
the supplier is not performing a public contract to the contracting authority’s satisfaction,

intro.p: where the supplier has breached the public contract, which of the following resulted from the breach—

content.p: partial termination of the public contract;
the award of damages;
a settlement agreement between the supplier and the contracting authority,

intro.p: where the supplier has breached the public contract, the date of any—

content.p: partial termination of the public contract,
award of damages, or
settlement,

where the supplier is not performing the public contract to the contracting authority’s satisfaction, the date when the contracting authority considered that the supplier had failed to improve its performance in accordance with section 71(4)(c),
an explanation of the nature of the contractual obligation which has been breached or is not being performed to the contracting authority’s satisfaction,

intro.p: an explanation of the nature of the breach or failure to perform including—

content.p: an explanation of the impact or consequences of the breach or failure to perform,
the duration of the breach or failure to perform and whether it is ongoing,
an explanation of any steps taken by the supplier to mitigate the impact or consequences of the breach or failure to perform,

intro.p: any steps that the contracting authority has taken to notify the supplier of the breach or failure to perform and encourage them to improve the situation, including—

content.p: any warning notices given under the public contract, or
any opportunity to improve performance,
what steps, if any, were taken by the supplier to improve the situation and why these were not sufficient,
where the breach has resulted in partial termination of the public contract, a description of which part of, or to what extent, the contract has been partially terminated, and

intro.p: where there has been an award of damages or payment of other monies following the breach or failure to perform—

content.p: confirmation that this is the case,
the amount of damages or other monies,

intro.p: the basis on which any damages were awarded or other monies paid, for example—

content.p: in the case of damages, in accordance with the public contract,
in the case of damages, in accordance with a decision of a court or tribunal, or
in the case of other monies, in accordance with a negotiated settlement, and
where there is a recorded decision of a court or tribunal finding that there was a breach, a link to the web page where the decision can be accessed or a copy of the decision.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.

This regulation does not apply to information required to be published in accordance with section 71(5) of the PA 2023 where a breach resulted in the full termination of a public contract (see instead regulation 41).

This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a contract change notice published under section 75(1) or (5) of the PA 2023
For provision which requires contracting authorities to publish contracts as modified or modifications in certain cases, see section 77 of the PA 2023..

intro.p: The information is—

the title of the procurement,
the unique identifier for the procurement,
the unique identifier for the contract,

intro.p: for each supplier party to the public contract or convertible contract—

content.p: the supplier’s name,
the supplier’s contact postal address and email address, and
the unique identifier for the supplier,

intro.p: whether the contracting authority is permitted to make the modification to the public contract or convertible contract because the modification is, by virtue of section 74(1)(a) of the PA 2023, one which is described—

content.p: in paragraphs 2 and 3 of Schedule 8 to that Act (urgency and the protection of life, etc),

in paragraph 8 of Schedule 8 to that Act (additional goods, services or works), or

wrapUp.p: (where the modification is permitted under one of those provisions),

content.p: an explanation of why the modification falls within one of the types of modifications mentioned in sub-paragraph (f),

intro.p: details of any change as a result of the modification—

content.p: to the estimated value of the public contract or convertible contract immediately prior to the modification, or
to the term of the public contract or convertible contract,

intro.p: where the modification is one which is described in paragraph 9 of Schedule 8 to that Act (transfer on corporate restructuring)—
for each new supplier that is party to the public contract or convertible contract—

content.p: the supplier’s name,
the supplier’s contact postal address and email address, and
the unique identifier for the supplier, and
for each supplier that will no longer be party to the public contract or convertible contract, the same information referred to in sub-paragraph (i)(aa) to (cc),

intro.p: the estimated date when—

content.p: the public contract or convertible contract will be modified, and
the modification will have effect, and
whether a voluntary standstill period applies in accordance with section 76(1) of the PA 2023 and, if so, the duration of that period.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.
This regulation sets out other information which must be included in a contract termination notice published under section 80(1) of the PA 2023.

intro.p: The information is—

content.p: the contracting authority information,
the title of the procurement,

intro.p: the unique identifier for—

content.p: the procurement,
the public contract,

intro.p: for each supplier party to the public contract—

content.p: the supplier’s name,
the supplier’s contact postal address and email address, and
the unique identifier for the supplier,
the reasons why the public contract has been terminated (including any reason mentioned in section 80(3) of the PA 2023),
the date when the public contract was terminated,
the estimated value of the public contract,

intro.p: where the termination of the public contract was the result of the supplier breaching the contract—

intro.p: whether the breach resulted in—

content.p: the award of damages;
a settlement agreement between the supplier and the contracting authority,

intro.p: the date of—

content.p: any award of any damages, or
any settlement,

where the supplier did not perform the public contract to the contracting authority’s satisfaction, the date when the contracting authority considered that the supplier had failed to improve its performance in accordance with section 71(4)(c),

intro.p: an explanation of the nature of the breach or failure to perform including—

the duration of the breach or failure to perform,

any steps that the contracting authority took to notify the supplier of the breach or failure to perform and encourage them to improve the situation, including any warning notices given under the public contract or other proper opportunity to improve performance pursuant to section 71(4)(b) of the PA 2023,
what steps, if any, were taken by the supplier to improve the situation and why these were not sufficient, and

intro.p: where there was an award of damages or other monies paid following the breach or failure to perform—

content.p: confirmation that this is the case,
the amount of damages or other monies paid,
the basis on which the damages were awarded or other monies paid, for example in accordance with the public contract, a decision of a court or tribunal or a negotiated settlement, and
where there is a recorded decision of a court or tribunal finding that there was a breach, a link to the web page where the decision can be accessed or a copy of the decision.
Nothing in this regulation prevents a contracting authority from publishing other information that relates to the same procurement in the notice.

part.heading: Other provisions supplementing the Procurement Act 2023

hcontainer.name: regulation
hcontainer.heading: Specification of light touch and reservable light touch services

content.p: For the purposes of section 9(1) of the PA 2023 (light touch contracts) the services which are covered by the CPV codes set out in column (1) of Table 1 in Schedule 1 and described in column (2) of that Table are specified as light touch services for the purposes of section 9(1) of the PA 2023.

For the purposes of section 33(7) of the PA 2023 (reserving contracts to public service mutuals), a service specified in columns (1) and (2) of Table 1 in Schedule 1 is specified as a reservable light touch service where in the entry corresponding to that service in column (3) the letter “R” appears.

The services which are covered by the CPV codes set out in Table 2 of Schedule 1 are specified as light touch services for the purposes of section 9(1) of the PA 2023, but only where those services are supplied under a contract for the supply of any thing listed in section 7(1)(a) to (f) of the PA 2023 (defence and security contracts).

p.ins: For the purposes of paragraph 2(2)(c) of Schedule 2 to the PA 2023 (exempted contracts), the calculation of the percentage of activities carried out by a person is to be made in accordance with this regulation.

Subject to paragraph (8), the percentage of activities carried out by a person for or on behalf of the contracting authorities or other persons described in sub-paragraph (ii) of paragraph 2(2)(c) is to be calculated by taking that person’s attributable turnover as a percentage of their total turnover, over the relevant period.
A person’s attributable turnover is their turnover deriving from activities carried out on behalf of the contracting authorities or other persons described in sub-paragraph (ii) of paragraph 2(2)(c).

Where a person’s attributable turnover or total turnover is not available for the entirety of the relevant period because the person was created or commenced their activities following the beginning of the relevant period, the attributable turnover and total turnover is to be calculated in accordance with paragraph (5).
A person’s attributable turnover and total turnover is to be calculated—
where there has been no turnover at all during the relevant period, using credible business projections for a period of three years beginning with the date of contract award;
in any other case, using—
any attributable turnover or total turnover, as the case may be, generated during the relevant period, and
credible business projections, for a period beginning with the date of contract award,
which, when combined, provide turnover information and projections for the entirety of the period of three years beginning with the date any turnover was first generated during the relevant period.

Where a person’s attributable turnover or total turnover for the entirety of the relevant period is, as at the date of contract award, no longer representative of the person’s activities because the activities changed as a result of a reorganisation of the person which occurred following the beginning of the relevant period, the attributable turnover and total turnover is to be calculated in accordance with paragraph (7).
A person’s attributable turnover and total turnover is to be calculated—
where there has been no turnover at all generated after reorganisation, using credible business projections for a period of three years beginning with the date of contract award;
in any other case, using—
any attributable turnover or total turnover, as the case may be, generated after reorganisation, and
credible business projections, for a period beginning with the date of contract award,
which, when combined, provide turnover information and projections for the entirety of the period of three years beginning with the date any turnover was first generated after reorganisation.

Where the percentage of activities carried out by a person calculated in accordance with paragraphs (2) to (7) does not satisfy the requirement in paragraph 2(2)(c) of Schedule 2 to the PA 2023, the percentage of activities may be calculated by taking, over the relevant period, any of the following that does satisfy that requirement—
costs incurred by the person on activities carried out for or on behalf of the authorities or other persons, as a percentage of their total costs;
time spent by the person on activities carried out for or on behalf of the authorities or other persons, as a percentage of their total time;
the value of goods, services or works supplied by the person to the authorities or other persons, as a percentage of the total value of goods, services or works supplied by the person;
the value of goods, services or works supplied to the person by the authorities or other persons, as a percentage of the total value of goods, services or works supplied to the person.
In this regulation—
” means a period in respect of which accounts are prepared in relation to the person;
” means the date when the contracting authority decided to award the contract;
” means—
the period of three years ending with the date of contract award, or

where, due to the timing of the preparation of the person’s accounts, information relating to turnover for the period in sub-paragraph (a) is not available as at the date of contract award, a period of three years ending with the date the last accounting period before the date of contract award for which such information is available ends;
” means a change, other than a minimal or incidental change, to a person’s structure, operations, funding or ownership.

For the purposes of paragraph 3(2)(b) of Schedule 2 to the PA 2023 (exempted contracts), the calculation of the percentage of activities contemplated by the horizontal arrangement is to be made in accordance with this regulation.

Subject to paragraph (8), the percentage of activities intended to be carried out other than for the purposes of the contracting authorities’ public functions is to be calculated by taking the non-attributable turnover generated by the horizontal arrangement’s activities as a percentage of the total turnover generated by the horizontal arrangement’s activities, over the relevant period.

A horizontal arrangement’s non-attributable turnover is turnover generated by the horizontal arrangement’s activities that is attributable to purposes other than the contracting authorities’ public functions.

Where the non-attributable turnover or total turnover generated by a horizontal arrangement’s activities is not available for the entirety of the relevant period because the arrangement was created, or the activities commenced, after the beginning of the relevant period, the non-attributable turnover and total turnover is to be calculated in accordance with paragraph (5).
Non-attributable turnover and total turnover generated by a horizontal arrangement’s activities is to be calculated—
where there has been no turnover at all during the relevant period, using credible business projections for a period of three years beginning with the date of contract award;
in any other case, using—

in any other case, using—
any non-attributable turnover or total turnover, as the case may be, generated after reorganisation or the change in activities, and
credible business projections, for a period beginning with the date of contract award,

costs incurred in respect of the horizontal arrangement’s activities for purposes other than the authorities’ public functions as a percentage of its total costs;
time spent in respect of the horizontal arrangement’s activities for purposes other than the authorities’ public functions as a percentage of its total time;

the value of goods, services or works supplied in respect of the horizontal arrangement’s activities for purposes other than the authorities’ public functions as a percentage of the total value of goods, services or works supplied in respect of the activities.
In this regulation—
” means a period in respect of which accounts are prepared in relation to the horizontal arrangement’s activities;

blockContainer.subheading: (This note is not part of the Regulations)

blockContainer.p: These Regulations supplement the Procurement Act 2023 (c. 54) (“PA 2023”).

Part 2 makes provision about the transparency of procurements carried out by contracting authorities under the PA 2023. Regulation 5 provides that certain notices, documents or information must be published or given by publishing them on the central digital platform which is an online system provided by the Minister for the Cabinet Office at the following website address: https://www.gov.uk/find-tender.

Regulations 6 and 7 make provision about how core supplier information (such as information about a supplier’s connected persons) is given to a contracting authority with a view to the award of a public contract. They provide that the authority must obtain confirmation that the supplier has shared that information through the central digital platform before a deadline. Regulations 9 to 12 set out what information is core supplier information.

Regulation 13 to 41 make provision about what information must be included in notices, documents or information which must be published under the PA 2023. In some cases, a provision sets out what other information must be included in addition to information which must be included in accordance with the PA 2023 itself. For example, regulation 17 sets out other information which must be included in a preliminary market engagement notice, in addition to the information which must be included in accordance with section 17(2)(a) of the PA 2023.
Part 3 makes provision which supplements the PA 2023 otherwise than in relation to transparency measures.

Regulation 42 and Schedule 1 specify the categories of services that qualify as “light touch” services for the purposes of sections 9 and 33 of the PA 2023. If a service is “light touch” it may be procured according to different rules from those that apply to the other types of contract whose procurement is covered by the PA 2023. These provisions also set out which of those services may be reserved such that a contracting authority may provide that only a qualifying public service mutual, as defined by the PA 2023, can bid for a contract for those services.

Regulation 43 disapplies the PA 2023 in respect of procurement by the NHS in England. The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 (S.I. 2023/1348) instead apply in this area.

Regulations 44 and 45 and Schedules 2 and 3 define the terms “central government authority” and “works” as they are used in the PA 2023. In Schedule 2, the entities defined as central government authorities are listed under the headings “lead authority” and “related authority” in order to provide consistency with the way the UK authorities covered by the WTO’s Agreement on Government Procurement are set out in the annexes to that agreement. As a result, entities may not always appear in alphabetical order. Regulation 46 defines the term “defence authority” as used in the PA 2023.

Part 4 of these Regulations contains amendments to the PA 2023. The amendments at regulation 47 insert into the PA 2023 new provisions which set out how that Act applies where a contracting authority which is a devolved Scottish authority wishes either to participate in a joint procurement or similar arrangement which is governed by the PA 2023, or to make use of a framework or dynamic market established under that Act.

Regulation 48 amends section 17 of the PA 2023 to disapply the requirement to publish a preiminary market engagement notice in respect of reserved and transferred Northern Ireland procurement by private utilities.
Part 5 makes provision about how these Regulations apply in relation to devolved Welsh authorities and devolved Scottish authorities.

An impact assessment in relation to the PA 2023 and associated reforms was published in May 2022 and can be found at https://bills.parliament.uk/publications/46429/documents/1767 or may obtained by writing to the Cabinet Office, 70 Whitehall, London, SW1A 2AS, United Kingdom.
